mhpfilter: Modified and Fully Modified Hodrick-Prescott Filters

Source: R/mhpfilter-package.R
mhpfilter-package.Rd

mhpfilter splits a macroeconomic time series into a trend and a cycle with the filter of Hodrick and Prescott (1997) and with two versions whose settings come from the data: the modified HP filter of McDermott (1997), which chooses the smoothing parameter of each series by generalised cross-validation (Choudhary, Hanif and Iqbal 2014), and the fully modified HP filter of Hanif, Iqbal and Choudhary (2017), which also reduces the bias of the HP filter at the ends of the series by raising the smoothing parameter there, with weights that minimise the end-point loss of Bloechl (2014).

Details

Functions, in the order of an analysis:

  • hp_filter, mhp_filter, fmhp_filter: the three filters.

  • mhp_batch, fmhp_batch: many series at once.

  • mhp_compare, batch_compare, fmhp_compare: the filters compared, by the moments of the cycles and the end-point loss.

  • hp_weights, hp_gain, hp_loss, hp_schedule: the weights, gains and end-point loss of any HP-type filter.

  • mhp_designs, mhp_simulate, fmhp_simulation: simulated series and the power comparison of the paper.

  • autoplot.mhp, plot_comparison, plot_batch: graphics; get_lambda, get_gcv: accessors.

  • mhp_interpret, mhp_cite: a plain-language interpretation and the references of a result; mhp_app: the built-in application.

Every filter is an S3 generic with a .default method. With as_dt = TRUE (the default) the filters return a data.table, as in version 0.1.0; with as_dt = FALSE a list with a class and the methods of mhp-methods. Utilities: mhp_theme, mhp_save, mhp_notation, mhp_reference.

Data. us_macro: quarterly real GDP, consumption and investment of the United States, 1959 to 2009.

Vignettes. Start with vignette("mhpfilter_01_getting_started", package = "mhpfilter"); browseVignettes("mhpfilter") lists all of them, in HTML and PDF.

Notation

Scalars are upper-case letters in normal face, indices lower-case italic, vectors lower-case bold and matrices upper-case bold; Greek letters follow the same rule. The full table is mhp_notation().

\(T\)number of observations
\(\mathbf{x}\), \(\mathbf{g}\), \(\mathbf{c}\)series, trend and cycle
\(\mathbf{K}\), \(\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{K}^\top\mathbf{K}\)second differences and the penalty matrix
\(\mathbf{B}\)smoother (filter weights)
\(\lambda\), \(\lambda_t\)smoothing parameter(s)
\(\alpha\), \(k\)end-point weight and number of end values
\(P_t(\omega)\), \(l(t)\), \(L\)gain, loss and total loss

References

Bloechl, A. (2014). Reducing the excess variability of the Hodrick-Prescott filter by flexible penalization. Discussion Paper 2014-1, University of Munich.

Choudhary, M. A., Hanif, M. N. and Iqbal, J. (2014). On smoothing macroeconomic time series using the modified HP filter. Applied Economics, 46(19), 2205–2214. doi:10.1080/00036846.2014.894631

Hanif, M. N., Iqbal, J. and Choudhary, M. A. (2017). Fully modified HP filter. SBP Working Paper Series, No. 88, State Bank of Pakistan.

Hodrick, R. J. and Prescott, E. C. (1997). Postwar U.S. business cycles: an empirical investigation. Journal of Money, Credit and Banking, 29(1), 1–16. doi:10.2307/2953682

McDermott, C. J. (1997). An automatic method for choosing the smoothing parameter in the HP filter. Unpublished, International Monetary Fund, Washington DC.
